title: Projection-neutral authoring and explicit capabilities

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Human-approved 30-slice rationale, ordering, verification, preservation boundary, deferrals, and stop conditions.

allowedWork: Repair classified verification ratchets, refactor development-only Article editor ownership, separate existing layout dependencies with geometry preservation, replace algebra registration side effects, update focused tests and durable project evidence.
Delete only superseded editor or registration modules after exact reachability proof.
disallowedWork: Do not modify user-owned economics Article source or generated publication.
No new layout experiment, layout retirement, aesthetic redesign, TypeScript or Python lesson, Graph3D promotion, SvelteKit migration, broad compatibility rewrite, or curriculum expansion.
goal: Restore an honest verification baseline, make economics whole-file Article editing projection-neutral, separate surviving scroll-layout implementations without retiring them, and replace algebra import-time choreography registration with explicit capabilities.
commitCadence: Commit after each independently verified slice.
stopConditions: Stop on an unexplained semantic or visual regression.
Stop if provenance becomes invalid or static and accessibility behavior is lost.
Stop if bundle growth is unbounded or a second clock, runtime, or editor authority would be required.
Stop when a subjective design decision is needed.
Stop if persistence cannot remain development-only and safe.
Stop when approved slices are exhausted or work would leave scope.

slices.summary: Established a green honest baseline: 4118/4118 tests, full typecheck, Svelte diagnostics, domain typecheck, generated publication freshness, production build, architecture gates, and Theseus validation all pass.

slices.title: Define economics Article-authoring descriptor
slices.summary: Added a pure Article authoring descriptor contract plus economics descriptor adapter over the existing source id, draft key, and semantic completions; no DOM, framework, compiler, or save authority moved into metadata.

slices.title: Adapt economics to shared whole-file editor
slices.summary: Added the economics adapter over the shared whole-file editor using the existing Article compiler, exact lock, semantic completions, local draft key, and capability-gated source-save endpoint; no editor or compiler fork was introduced.

slices.title: Move editor lifecycle to route capability
slices.summary: Moved the lazily loaded whole-file editor session and forced disposal into the economics route capability; the toolbar now invokes an explicit editArticle callback instead of querying presenter DOM.

slices.title: Expose Edit article from every economics projection
slices.summary: Enabled the single route-owned Edit article action in all six economics views; the contribution test now ratchets projection-wide availability.

slices.title: Preserve semantic reveal and focus
slices.summary: The route captures the active semantic passage before opening authoring and reveals its Article directive id; malformed or unavailable ids fall back to #context.

slices.title: Preview valid edits through active projection
slices.summary: Valid drafts now compile into route-owned publication state and remount the active published or presenter projection with semantic handoff; invalid drafts never replace the last valid view.

slices.title: Preserve Vim write and quit commands
slices.summary: Ratcheted all four canonical Vim commands through the shared draft session and single CodeMirror runtime; dirty-buffer refusal and persistence-failure behavior remain covered.

slices.title: Remove two-column passage-editor state
slices.summary: Removed the presenter-local passage buffer, modal state, dynamic component loader, edit buttons, geometry refresh path, and scroll pause; Two Columns now renders the compiled publication like every other projection.

slices.title: Delete superseded economics passage editor
slices.summary: Deleted the unreachable KpEconomicsPassageEditor component and its dedicated stylesheet; exact source search, stylesheet ownership, architecture-adjacent tests, and full typing are green.

slices.title: Pressure editor across layouts and viewports
slices.summary: Replaced the obsolete passage-editor suite with ten browser checks spanning every economics projection, live last-valid preview, Vim persistence without reload, and phone plus short-viewport containment.

slices.title: Audit Inline Sticky and Two Columns dependency seam
slices.summary: Added an executable seam inventory covering the one direct stylesheet import, six inherited geometry selectors, three inherited tokens, the shared cue hook, and the intentional mobile single-column fallback.

slices.title: Extract projection-neutral shared geometry
slices.summary: Renamed the inherited layout owner to economics-demand-shift-scroll-passage.css and updated both presenter capabilities plus preservation inventories; selector and value geometry is unchanged.

slices.title: Extract projection-neutral responsive tokens
slices.summary: All shared scroll-passage geometry now consumes neutral --kp-scroll-passage-* tokens; dependent lesson, responsive, and desktop Two Columns rules use the same values with no legacy token references.

slices.title: Remove Two Columns dependency on Inline Sticky CSS
slices.summary: The executable seam is now symmetric: Inline Sticky and Two Columns each directly import the neutral scroll-passage owner, and no Inline Sticky-named stylesheet exists or appears in either capability.

slices.title: Add neutral layout hook contract
slices.summary: The shared cue contract is now data-kp-scroll-passage-cue in the Svelte renderer, neutral/base/responsive/Two Columns CSS, seam inventory, and Inline Sticky browser check; no legacy cue hook remains.

slices.title: Re-audit fresh layout reachability without retirement
slices.summary: The fresh audited path confirms Inline Sticky remains canonical, dynamically loadable, toolbar-visible, browser-tested, and independent of Two Columns; the durable verdict is retain, not retire.
